lines.text: That taco place was elite, no cap. Lowkey the best meal I've had all year.
lines.ko: 그 타코집 최고였어, 진짜로. 은근히 올해 먹은 것 중 최고야.

lines.text: Wait, slow down. 'No cap' means you're serious, and 'lowkey' means kind of?
lines.ko: 잠깐, 천천히. 'no cap'은 진심이고 'lowkey'는 좀 그렇다는 거지?

lines.text: Exactly. And 'elite' just means really, really good.
lines.ko: 정확해. 그리고 'elite'는 그냥 엄청 좋다는 뜻이야.

lines.text: Okay, then I'm highkey jealous. Take me there on Friday.
lines.ko: 좋아, 그럼 대놓고 부럽다. 금요일에 나 데려가.

questions.q: How does the second speaker feel?
When do they plan to go?

lines.text: I told my sister I couldn't come to dinner, and she just replied 'k.' Is that bad?
lines.ko: 언니한테 저녁 못 간다고 했더니 'k.'만 왔어. 안 좋은 거야?

lines.text: With a full stop? That's cold. She's definitely annoyed.
lines.ko: 마침표까지? 차갑네. 확실히 짜증 났어.

lines.text: Ugh. If she'd written 'okay!' with an exclamation mark, I'd be fine, right?
lines.ko: 으. 느낌표 붙여서 'okay!'라고 했으면 괜찮은 거지?

lines.text: Totally fine. Call her instead of texting. Tone is easier on the phone.
lines.ko: 완전 괜찮지. 문자 말고 전화해. 전화가 톤 전달이 쉬워.

questions.q: What does the friend think the reply means?

lines.text: Fancy a barbie this arvo, mate? I'll shout the snags.
lines.ko: 오늘 오후 바비큐 어때, 친구? 소시지는 내가 쏠게.

lines.text: Barbie is barbecue, arvo is afternoon, and snags are sausages. Did I get that right?
lines.ko: barbie는 바비큐, arvo는 오후, snags는 소시지. 맞게 이해했어?

lines.text: Spot on! You're basically a local now.
lines.ko: 정확해! 이제 거의 현지인이네.

lines.text: Heaps good. I'll bring the drinks. No worries.
lines.ko: 완전 좋아. 음료는 내가 가져갈게. 걱정 마.

questions.q: What will the second speaker bring?

lines.text: So how was the date? You were so excited.
lines.ko: 그래서 데이트 어땠어? 엄청 기대했잖아.

lines.text: Great until he sent his soup back three times. I got the ick.
lines.ko: 수프를 세 번이나 돌려보내기 전까진 좋았어. 정떨어졌어.

lines.text: Three times? That's not tiny. That's a red flag.
lines.ko: 세 번? 그건 사소한 게 아니지. 위험 신호야.

lines.text: Exactly. I'm not seeing him again, but the dessert was amazing.
lines.ko: 그러니까. 다시 안 만날 건데 디저트는 끝내줬어.

options: Sent his soup back three times

questions.q: What was good about the date?

lines.text: I asked Liam if he'd cover my shift, and he said 'yeah, no'. Is that a yes?
lines.ko: 리엄한테 내 근무 대신해 줄 수 있냐고 물었더니 'yeah, no'래. 그거 '응'이야?

lines.text: That's a no. The 'yeah' just means he heard you.
lines.ko: 그건 '아니'야. 'yeah'는 그냥 들었다는 뜻이야.

lines.text: And if he'd said 'no, yeah'?
lines.ko: 그럼 'no, yeah'라고 했으면?

lines.text: Then it'd be a yes. Always listen to the last word.
lines.ko: 그럼 '응'이지. 항상 마지막 단어를 들어.

questions.q: What did the man ask Liam?
Which word gives the real answer?

lines.text: You look knackered. Rough day?
lines.ko: 녹초 같아 보여. 힘든 하루였어?

lines.text: Absolutely rubbish. My train was cancelled and I missed the meeting. Gutted.
lines.ko: 완전 최악이었어. 기차 취소돼서 회의 놓쳤어. 속상해.

lines.text: Fancy a cuppa and a biscuit? That fixes most things.
lines.ko: 차 한잔에 비스킷 어때? 그거면 웬만한 건 해결돼.

lines.text: Cheers. You're a lifesaver.
lines.ko: 고마워. 넌 구세주야.

questions.q: Why did the woman miss the meeting?

lines.text: My new coworker said we should totally hang out sometime. Do you think she meant it?
lines.ko: 새 동료가 언젠가 꼭 놀자고 했어. 진심이었을까?

lines.text: Maybe, maybe not. 'Sometime' is often just a polite way to end a conversation.
lines.ko: 그럴 수도, 아닐 수도. '언젠가'는 대화를 끝내는 예의 바른 말일 때가 많아.

lines.text: So how do I find out?
lines.ko: 그럼 어떻게 알아내?

lines.text: Suggest something specific, like lunch on Wednesday. Her answer will tell you everything.
lines.ko: 수요일 점심처럼 구체적으로 제안해 봐. 대답이 모든 걸 말해 줄 거야.

questions.q: Who said 'we should hang out sometime'?

options: A polite way to end a conversation

lines.text: So, how much did your new car cost? Must have been loads.
lines.ko: 그래서 새 차 얼마였어? 엄청 비쌌겠다.

lines.text: Ha, less than my coffee habit, probably. How's your garden coming along?
lines.ko: 하, 아마 내 커피값보다 덜할걸. 너네 정원은 어떻게 돼 가?

lines.text: Oh, don't get me started. The tomatoes are a disaster.
lines.ko: 아, 말도 마. 토마토가 엉망이야.

lines.text: No! Tell me everything.
lines.ko: 말도 안 돼! 다 얘기해 봐.

lines.text: Welcome back to Say What, the podcast that explains the slang your younger coworkers use.
lines.ko: 젊은 동료들이 쓰는 슬랭을 설명하는 팟캐스트 '세이 왓'에 다시 오신 걸 환영해요.

lines.text: Today's words are 'mid', which means average, and 'the ick', a sudden feeling of disgust over something small.
lines.ko: 오늘의 단어는 평범하다는 뜻의 'mid'와 사소한 일로 갑자기 정떨어지는 느낌인 'the ick'이에요.

lines.text: Use them carefully at work. Calling your boss's presentation mid is not a career move.
lines.ko: 회사에선 조심해서 쓰세요. 상사 발표를 mid라고 하는 건 커리어에 도움이 안 돼요.

options: Be careful using slang at work

lines.text: In text messages, punctuation works like tone of voice.
lines.ko: 문자에서 문장 부호는 목소리 톤처럼 작동해요.

lines.text: A single 'k' with a full stop can feel cold, while 'okay!' with an exclamation mark feels warm and friendly.
lines.ko: 마침표 찍은 'k' 하나는 차갑게, 느낌표 붙은 'okay!'는 따뜻하고 친근하게 느껴져요.

lines.text: If a conversation is getting tense, switch to a phone call. It's much harder to misunderstand someone's voice.
lines.ko: 대화가 긴장되면 전화로 바꾸세요. 목소리는 오해하기가 훨씬 어려워요.

questions.q: What does punctuation work like in texts?
What should you do if a conversation gets tense?

lines.text: Moving to the UK? Here are three words you'll hear every day.
lines.ko: 영국으로 이사 가세요? 매일 듣게 될 세 단어를 알려 드릴게요.

lines.text: 'Cheers' means thanks as often as it means a toast, 'knackered' means exhausted, and 'gutted' means bitterly disappointed.
lines.ko: 'cheers'는 건배만큼 자주 '고마워'를 뜻하고, 'knackered'는 녹초, 'gutted'는 몹시 실망했다는 뜻이에요.

lines.text: And if someone offers you a cuppa, they mean a cup of tea, and saying no is rarely an option.
lines.ko: 그리고 누가 cuppa를 권하면 차 한 잔이고, 거절은 거의 불가능해요.

questions.q: Besides a toast, what does 'cheers' often mean?

lines.text: American English changes a lot from region to region.
lines.ko: 미국 영어는 지역마다 많이 달라요.

lines.text: In the South you'll hear 'y'all' for 'you all' and 'fixin' to' for 'about to', while many New Yorkers stand 'on line' instead of 'in line'.
lines.ko: 남부에선 'you all' 대신 'y'all', '막 ~하려던 참' 대신 'fixin' to'를 듣고, 뉴요커들은 'in line' 대신 'on line'에 서요.

lines.text: None of these are mistakes. They're local habits, and using them well will make people smile.
lines.ko: 이건 실수가 아니라 지역 습관이고, 잘 쓰면 사람들이 미소 지을 거예요.

questions.q: How does the speaker describe these expressions?

lines.text: When native speakers talk fast, 'going to' becomes 'gonna', 'want to' becomes 'wanna', and 'what do you' becomes 'whaddya'.
lines.ko: 원어민이 빨리 말하면 'going to'는 'gonna', 'want to'는 'wanna', 'what do you'는 'whaddya'가 돼요.

lines.text: That's why you might understand films with subtitles but struggle in real conversations.
lines.ko: 그래서 자막 있는 영화는 알아들어도 실제 대화에선 힘들 수 있어요.

lines.text: Try shadowing short clips daily, copying the rhythm rather than each word.
lines.ko: 매일 짧은 영상을 따라 말해 보세요. 단어 하나하나보다 리듬을 따라 하세요.

questions.q: What does 'what do you' become in fast speech?
Why might real conversations be hard?
options: Words blur together when spoken fast
There are no subtitles in books

questions.q: What does the speaker recommend copying?

lines.text: Not everything people say is meant literally.
lines.ko: 사람들이 하는 말이 모두 문자 그대로는 아니에요.

lines.text: 'How are you?' in a shop is just hello, 'we should hang out sometime' may only be polite, and 'I'll think about it' often means no.
lines.ko: 가게에서 'How are you?'는 그냥 인사이고, '언젠가 놀자'는 예의일 수 있고, '생각해 볼게'는 종종 거절이에요.

lines.text: The trick is to look for follow-up: real interest comes with questions, dates, and next steps.
lines.ko: 요령은 후속 행동을 보는 거예요. 진짜 관심엔 질문, 날짜, 다음 단계가 따라와요.

questions.q: What does 'How are you?' in a shop usually mean?
What does 'I'll think about it' often mean?

lines.text: Today's idioms are all about decisions.
lines.ko: 오늘의 관용구는 모두 결정에 관한 거예요.

lines.text: If you're 'on the fence', you haven't decided. If you 'bite the bullet', you do something unpleasant you've been avoiding.
lines.ko: 'on the fence'면 아직 결정 못 한 거고, 'bite the bullet'은 피해 온 싫은 일을 해내는 거예요.

lines.text: And when 'the ball's in your court', it's your turn to act, so stop waiting for someone else.
lines.ko: 그리고 'the ball's in your court'면 당신이 행동할 차례니까 다른 사람을 기다리지 마세요.

questions.q: What should you do when the ball's in your court?

lines.text: Welcome to Canada in January. Temperatures can drop to minus thirty, so dress in layers.
lines.ko: 1월의 캐나다에 오신 걸 환영해요. 기온이 영하 30도까지 떨어질 수 있으니 겹쳐 입으세요.

lines.text: You'll need a toque, which is a warm knitted hat, and you'll probably be offered a double-double, a coffee with two creams and two sugars.
lines.ko: 따뜻한 털모자인 toque가 필요하고, 크림 둘 설탕 둘 커피인 더블더블을 권유받을 거예요.

lines.text: And yes, people really do say 'eh' at the end of sentences. It's friendly, eh?
lines.ko: 그리고 네, 사람들은 정말로 문장 끝에 'eh'를 붙여요. 친근하죠, eh?
